# Turisync

> Travel tech analysis: AI in travel, distribution, hotel, airline and port tech, startups and funding. / Análisis de travel tech: IA en viajes, distribución, tecnología hotelera, aérea y portuaria, startups e inversión.

Bilingual travel-tech publication (English first; Spanish 24 h later). Publishes Tuesdays and Thursdays at 8:00 am ET.

## EN
- [Nichupté bridge, six months in: an 11.2 km link that reshapes Cancún's airport and hotel-zone traffic](https://www.turisync.net/articles/nichupte-bridge-six-months-in-an-11-2-km.md): The bridge over Laguna Nichupté opened May 2, 2026, with three lanes, a cycle path, solar panels and capacity for 12,000 vehicles a day. What it changes for ground transport operators.
- [The Mexican Caribbean's AI gap: hotels use chatbots, but few build their own systems](https://www.turisync.net/articles/mexican-caribbeans-ai-gap-hotels-use-chatbots-but-few.md): Only four in ten tourism companies in the region invest in technology, and a local tech director warns guests will notice the AI gap within 24 months. Where the opportunity is.
- [Visitax goes digital: what Quintana Roo's shift away from airport collection means for travel platforms](https://www.turisync.net/articles/visitax-goes-digital-what-quintana-roos-shift-away-from.md): Quintana Roo plans to end in-person collection of its 293-peso visitor fee at Cancún airport. Hoteliers report demands more than 80% above the fee. The integration opportunity for OTAs and airlines.
- [Cancún airport's biometric e-gates: 40 planned, 30 eligible countries and a digital FMM](https://www.turisync.net/articles/cancun-airports-biometric-e-gates-40-planned-30-eligible.md): Cancún is scaling automated immigration from 26 to 40 e-gates and from 48 to 54 manual booths. Who can use them and why it matters for peak-season throughput.
- [The sargassum tech stack: how satellites, ocean models and drones now track the Mexican Caribbean's biggest risk](https://www.turisync.net/articles/sargassum-tech-stack-how-satellites-ocean-models-and-drones.md): NOAA's risk tool went daily at 1 km resolution in 2026, and UNAM reads Sentinel-2 imagery every five days. What the monitoring stack can and cannot do for hotels and tour operators.
- [Mexico's first cruise home port: the tech stack a turnaround terminal needs](https://www.turisync.net/articles/vallarta-home-port-tech-stack.md): Puerto Vallarta will host Mexico's first cruise home port. Turning a port of call into a turnaround terminal is as much a systems project as a construction one. Here's the stack to watch.

## ES
- [El primer home port de México: la tecnología que necesita una terminal de salida de cruceros](https://www.turisync.net/es/articulos/vallarta-home-port-stack.md): Puerto Vallarta será el primer home port de México. Convertir un puerto de escala en terminal de salida es tanto un proyecto de sistemas como de obra. Esta es la tecnología a seguir.
